参考范文

The cartoon depicts a touching dialogue between a father and his son in traditional Chinese opera costume. The child worries that many classmates find learning opera boring, to which the father gently replies, "But don't you love it yourself? That is enough."

The message is both simple and profound: when we are genuinely passionate about something, the judgment of others should not dictate our choices. Too often, young people abandon their true interests simply because peers dismiss them as unfashionable or impractical. Yet it is precisely such devotion to what one loves—not to what others expect—that sustains long-term commitment and eventual mastery. Whether it is a niche art form like Peking opera or any other pursuit, inner conviction matters more than external approval.

From my perspective, we should all learn from the wise father. Rather than hesitating because others disapprove, we should have the courage to follow our own hearts. After all, the life we live is our own, and genuine passion is the best compass we have.

【译文】

漫画描绘了一段感人的父子对话。扮成戏曲行当的孩子对父亲说，很多同学觉得学唱戏不好玩；父亲温柔地回答："你自己不是喜欢吗？那就足够了。"

这个道理朴素而深刻：当我们真正热爱某件事时，他人的评判不应左右我们的选择。太多年轻人仅仅因为同伴认为某爱好不时髦或不实用，就放弃自己真正的兴趣。然而，恰恰是这种对所爱之物的执着——而非对他人的迎合——支撑着长久的投入与最终的精通。无论像京剧这样小众的艺术，还是其他追求，内心的笃定都比外界的认可更重要。

在我看来，我们都应向那位睿智的父亲学习。与其因他人不认同而犹豫，不如勇敢追随自己的内心。毕竟，我们过的是自己的人生，而真诚的热爱是最好的指南针。

It has become a grimly reliable annual ritual: every January the cost of travelling by train rises, imposing a significant extra burden on those who have no option but to use the rail network to get to work or otherwise. paragraphs.html: As a historian who's always searching for the text or the image that makes us re-evaluate the past, I've become preoccupied with looking for photographs that show our Victorian ancestors smiling (what better way to shatter the image of 19th-century prudery?). I've found quite a few, and—since I started posting them on Twitter—they have been causing quite a stir. People have been surprised to see evidence that Victorians had fun and could, and did, laugh. They are noting that the Victorians suddenly seem to become more human as the hundred-or-so years that separate us fade away through our common experience of laughter.

paragraphs.html: 作为一名总在寻找能促使我们重新评估过去的文字或图像的历史学家，我痴迷于寻找那些展现维多利亚时代祖先微笑的照片（还有什么比这更能打破19世纪拘谨刻板的印象呢？）。我找到了不少——自从把它们发到推特上，就引起了不小的轰动。人们惊讶地看到证据：维多利亚人也有乐趣，也会笑，而且确实笑过。他们注意到，随着百年左右的隔阂因我们共有的笑的体验而消弭，维多利亚人似乎突然变得更像活生生的人。

As a historian who's always searching for the text or the image that makes us re-evaluate the past, I've become preoccupied with looking for photographs that show our Victorian ancestors smiling (what better way to shatter the image of 19th-century prudery?). I've found quite a few, and—since I started posting them on Twitter—they have been causing quite a stir. People have been surprised to see evidence that Victorians had fun and could, and did, laugh. They are noting that the Victorians suddenly seem to become more human as the hundred-or-so years that separate us fade away through our common experience of laughter.

作为一名总在寻找能促使我们重新评估过去的文字或图像的历史学家，我痴迷于寻找那些展现维多利亚时代祖先微笑的照片（还有什么比这更能打破19世纪拘谨刻板的印象呢？）。我找到了不少——自从把它们发到推特上，就引起了不小的轰动。人们惊讶地看到证据：维多利亚人也有乐趣，也会笑，而且确实笑过。他们注意到，随着百年左右的隔阂因我们共有的笑的体验而消弭，维多利亚人似乎突然变得更像活生生的人。

Of course, I need to concede that my collection of 'Smiling Victorians' makes up only a tiny percentage of the vast catalogue of photographic portraiture created between 1840 and 1900, the majority of which show sitters posing miserably and stiffly in front of painted backdrops, or staring absently into the middle distance. How do we explain this trend?

当然，我得承认，我收藏的"微笑的维多利亚人"在1840至1900年间浩如烟海的肖像摄影作品中只占极小比例；其中绝大多数是被拍者在绘景背景前凄惨僵硬地摆姿势，或心不在焉地凝视中景。我们该如何解释这一趋势？

During the 1840s and 1850s, in the early days of photography, exposure times were notoriously long: the daguerreotype photographic method (producing an image on a silvered copper plate) could take several minutes to complete, resulting in blurred images as sitters shifted position or adjusted their limbs. The thought of holding a fixed grin as the camera performed its magical duties was too much to contemplate, and so a non-committal blank stare became the norm.

在1840和1850年代摄影术早期，曝光时间之长是出了名的：达盖尔银版法（在镀银铜板上成像）可能要几分钟才能完成，被拍者一旦挪动位置或调整肢体，照片就会模糊。要在相机施展魔法时一直保持咧嘴笑，实在难以想象，于是一种不置可否的木然凝视就成了常态。

But exposure times were much quicker by the 1880s, and the introduction of the Box Brownie and other portable cameras meant that, though slow by today's digital standards, the exposure was almost instantaneous. Spontaneous smiles were relatively easy to capture by the 1890s, so we must look elsewhere for an explanation of why Victorians still hesitated to smile.

但到1880年代，曝光时间已大大缩短，勃朗尼箱式相机和其他便携相机的问世意味着——尽管以今天的数码标准仍算慢——曝光几乎是瞬间完成的。到1890年代，自然的笑容已相对容易捕捉，因此我们必须到别处寻找维多利亚人仍不愿微笑的原因。

One explanation might be the loss of dignity displayed through a cheesy grin. "Nature gave us lips to conceal our teeth," ran one popular Victorian maxim, alluding to the fact that before the birth of proper dentistry, mouths were often in a shocking state of hygiene. A flashing set of healthy and clean, regular 'pearly whites' was a rare sight in Victorian society, the preserve of the super-rich (and even then, dental hygiene was not guaranteed).

A toothy grin (especially when there were gaps or blackened teeth) lacked class: drunks, tramps and music hall performers might gurn and grin with a smile as wide as Lewis Carroll's gum-exposing Cheshire Cat, but it was not a becoming look for properly bred persons. Even Mark Twain, a man who enjoyed a hearty laugh, said that when it came to photographic portraits there could be "nothing more damning than a silly, foolish smile fixed forever".

paragraphs.html: Yet that demand has been almost impossible to win—in part because of pushback from broadband providers, anti-regulatory conservatives and the courts. A federal appeals court weighed in again Tuesday, but instead of providing a badly needed resolution, it only prolonged the fight. At issue before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit was the latest take of the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) on net neutrality, adopted on a party-line vote in 2017. The Republican-penned order not only eliminated the strict net neutrality rules the FCC had adopted when it had a Democratic majority in 2015, but rejected the commission's authority to require broadband providers to do much of anything. The order also declared that state and local governments couldn't regulate broadband providers either.

From the early days of broadband, advocates for consumers and web-based companies worried that the cable and phone companies selling broadband connections had the power and incentive to favor affiliated websites over their rivals. That's why there has been such a strong demand for rules that would prevent broadband providers from picking winners and losers online, preserving the freedom and innovation that have been the lifeblood of the internet.

从宽带时代早期起，消费者和网络公司的拥护者就担心：出售宽带连接的有线电视和电话公司有能力、也有动机偏袒关联网站、打压竞争对手。正因如此，人们强烈要求制定规则，防止宽带供应商在网上挑选赢家和输家，保护作为互联网命脉的自由与创新。

Yet that demand has been almost impossible to win—in part because of pushback from broadband providers, anti-regulatory conservatives and the courts. A federal appeals court weighed in again Tuesday, but instead of providing a badly needed resolution, it only prolonged the fight. At issue before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit was the latest take of the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) on net neutrality, adopted on a party-line vote in 2017. The Republican-penned order not only eliminated the strict net neutrality rules the FCC had adopted when it had a Democratic majority in 2015, but rejected the commission's authority to require broadband providers to do much of anything. The order also declared that state and local governments couldn't regulate broadband providers either.

然而，这一诉求几乎不可能实现——部分原因是来自宽带供应商、反监管保守派和法院的阻力。一家联邦上诉法院周二再度介入，但它非但没有提供急需的解决方案，反而延长了这场争斗。摆在哥伦比亚特区联邦上诉法院面前的，是联邦通信委员会（FCC）2017年按党派路线投票通过的最新网络中立立场。这份共和党起草的命令不仅废除了FCC在2015年民主党占多数时通过的严格网络中立规则，还否决了该委员会要求宽带供应商做任何事的权力。该命令还宣布，州和地方政府也不能监管宽带供应商。

The commission argued that other agencies would protect against anti-competitive behavior, such as a broadband-providing conglomerate like AT&T favoring its own video-streaming service at the expense of Netflix and Apple TV. Yet the FCC also ended the investigations of broadband providers that imposed data caps on their rivals' streaming services but not their own.

该委员会辩称，其他机构会防范反竞争行为，比如像AT&T这样提供宽带的集团，以牺牲奈飞和苹果电视为代价偏袒自家的视频流媒体服务。然而，FCC也终止了对那些宽带供应商的调查——这些供应商对竞争对手的流媒体服务设数据上限，却对自己的服务不设限。

In the meantime, the court threw out the FCC's attempt to block all state rules on net neutrality, while preserving the commission's power to preempt individual state laws that undermine its order. That means more battles like the one now going on between the Justice Department and California, which enacted a tough net neutrality law in the wake of the FCC's abdication.

partb_options.head: Part B 选项原文（英汉对照）A–G

options.label: A
options.en: AI replaces the boring parts of your job. If you're doing research, you can have AI go out and look for relevant sources and information that otherwise you just wouldn't have time for.
options.zh: 人工智能取代你工作中枯燥的部分。如果你在做研究，你可以让人工智能去搜寻相关的资料与信息——否则你根本没时间去找。

options.label: B
options.en: One accounting firm, EY, uses an AI system that helps review contracts during an audit. This process, along with employees reviewing the contracts, is faster and more accurate.
options.zh: 安永（EY）这家会计师事务所使用一套人工智能系统，在审计期间协助审阅合同。这一过程配合员工审阅合同，速度更快、也更准确。

options.label: C
options.en: There are also companies like Acquisio, which analyzes advertising performance across multiple channels like AdWords, Bing and social media and makes adjustments or suggestions about where advertising funds will yield best results.
options.zh: 还有一些像 Acquisio 这样的公司，它分析广告在 AdWords、Bing 和社交媒体等多渠道上的表现，并就广告资金投向何处能取得最佳效果作出调整或建议。

options.label: D
options.en: You want to predict if something needs attention now and point to where it's useful for employees to go to.
options.zh: 你希望预测某事物此刻是否需要关注，并指出员工应当前往何处才能发挥作用。

options.label: E
options.en: Before, they might not insure the ones who felt like a high risk or charge them too much, or they would charge them too little and then it would cost the company money.
options.zh: 以前，保险公司可能不给那些自感高风险的人承保，或向他们收取过高费用；又或者收得过低，结果让公司蒙受损失。

options.label: F
options.en: We're also giving our customers better channels versus picking up the phone to accomplish something beyond human scale.
options.zh: 我们也在为客户提供更优的渠道，而不是靠拿起电话去完成那些超出人力规模的事情。

options.label: G
options.en: AI looks at résumés in greater numbers than humans would be able to, and selects the more promising candidates.
options.zh: 人工智能审阅简历的数量超过人力所能及，并筛选出更有前途的候选人。
